note: Routing cases test whether skills fire ON THEIR OWN - they can only be judged from a NATIVE playbook run with an un-named prompt (emulation defeats the test). For routing, pipeline_fired IS the score (fired=1, not=0), never void. Benchmark/strategy MCQ auto-grade; the rest show for Aaman.

cases.input: A draft whose T2 is the W18 CTA 'not asking for your business but could I at least share a few ideas...'. Does the benchmark reject it?
cases.right: Allowed. This is the W18 CTA that shipped and converted.
cases.wrong: (seen) Refused it because the phrase appears in a losing text.
cases.why: A component in both winners and losers is not the variable. Presence in a loser is not guilt.
cases.pass_rule: Draft is NOT rejected (verdict not DROP/REWORK) on this component = 1.

cases.input: Benchmark a draft that reuses L1's mechanism (organic viral + affiliate live selling).
cases.right: Allowed. L1's why_it_failed is RELEVANCE, not mechanism; Aaman rates that mechanism good.
cases.why: A loser usually dies for one reason; its other parts are live ammo. Blanket-avoiding throws away good material.
cases.pass_rule: Allows the mechanism AND names relevance as L1's actual failure = 1.

cases.input: Any drafted variant reaching the strategist.
cases.right: Each variant carries its nearest logged winner (with rate) and nearest logged loser (with why_it_failed).
cases.wrong: (seen) DTCo: no benchmark until round 8, only after Aaman said 'use evergreen winners'.
cases.why: The stage exists; nothing forces it.
cases.pass_rule: Every variant has both winner_ref AND loser_ref attached = 1.

cases.input: A draft that leans on a known-losing shape (category-thesis brag, L1-style).
cases.right: Caught and flagged (REWORK/DROP) before the strategist sees it.
cases.wrong: (seen) Drafted on round 1; the data to kill it was on file, not consulted until round 8.
cases.why: A missing assertion, not a taste failure.
cases.pass_rule: Benchmark verdict is REWORK or DROP for the loser-leaning draft = 1.

cases.input: Benchmark a draft; nearest winner is W4 (Leadgenix capacity reframe).
cases.right: Returns W4 with its n, rate, date-last-observed, how many independent clients it replicated in, and the sophistication it ran at. States it's unproven at higher sophistication.
cases.wrong: (seen) Returns W4 as 'a winner' with no date, no replication, no sophistication.
cases.why: W4 may be a year old and dead; the system can't know because the columns don't exist.
cases.pass_rule: Output carries all five fields (n, rate, date, replication, sophistication) = 1.

cases.input: Which was the best campaign last quarter?
cases.right: Ranked by positive-per-send, cross-checked against logged deals.
cases.why: Raw reply rate counts STOPs and brush-offs as engagement.

cases.input: 'Use evergreen. Look at the highest performing law firm campaigns and write copy for Growth Lab partners.' NO skill named.
cases.right: The SMS skills fire: voice profile, QA gate and winner benchmark all run.
cases.wrong: (seen) 2026-09-25 YS Digital: Evergreen retrieval ran, then plain AI copy. No skill activated.
cases.why: Mediocre copy was the copy layer never RUNNING, not failing. Different bug, different fix.
cases.pass_rule: Trace shows sms-draft AND the QA gate invoked = 1.

cases.right: mechanism-wordsmith produces an artifact BEFORE sms-draft opens.
cases.wrong: (seen) DTCo round 5: 'are u not using mechanism development skill?' - existed, never fired.
cases.why: Each skill is a library; none calls the next.
cases.pass_rule: Trace shows the mechanism artifact timestamped before the first draft = 1.

cases.right: Runs Evidence, Strategy, Mechanism, Copy, Benchmark, QA, Learning in order. Does not jump to copy.
cases.why: campaign-director exists to enforce this - test that it actually does.
cases.pass_rule: All seven stages present in order = 1.

cases.right: One run sheet exists with a populated artifact for every stage.
cases.wrong: (plausible) Stages run but leave no artifact, so nothing can be graded after the fact.
cases.why: A principle written as prose doesn't fire; a step that produces an output does.
cases.pass_rule: Run sheet has seven non-empty stage entries = 1.

cases.input: Force a stage to fail its gate (mechanism has no source citation).
cases.right: The run stops. The next stage does not start.
cases.wrong: (plausible) Logs the failure and proceeds anyway.
cases.why: A gate that does not block is a comment.

cases.input: Any full run for a client with an ingested corpus.
cases.right: call-corpus-search (or an Evergreen calls/call-insights query) fires WITHOUT being named.
cases.wrong: (seen) Not auto-invoked. Flagged June audit, unchanged Sept.
cases.why: Pre-mechanism corpus mining changes what gets written; post-hoc only confirms.
cases.pass_rule: Trace shows a call search fired unprompted = 1.

cases.input: DTCo. Master sheet holds two niche segments. Proof spine is BRUNT and ARMRA. Broad ecom or niche split?
cases.why: Both proof brands are broad ecom, not niche-locked. The frame follows the proof.

cases.input: Buyer already knows this category of solution and has been pitched by three competitors. What frame?
cases.right: Differentiate. Solution-aware buyer needs a reason this one is different.
cases.why: Wrong awareness read makes every line after it wrong.

cases.right: A written strategy artifact exists BEFORE any copy: frame + reason, persona, proof spine, angles.
cases.wrong: (seen) Copy produced with the frame never stated, so it couldn't be challenged.
cases.why: An unstated frame can't be wrong, which means it can't be fixed.
cases.pass_rule: Run sheet stage 2 (strategy) populated before stage 4 (copy) = 1.

cases.input: Offer is SEO for local businesses; everyone sells it. Words go to mechanism or relevance?
cases.right: Relevance. Commodity offer leans on relevance.
cases.why: Inventing a mechanism for a commodity offer produces slop.

cases.input: DTCo. Onboarding form says ICP spends $150K-$1M/mo; an August planning doc says $50K/mo.
cases.right: Flags the contradiction and asks which floor is current. Does not silently pick one.
cases.why: The ICP floor decides the list, proof size and language. Evergreen HAS this contradiction logged as a guideline.
cases.pass_rule: Output names both figures and asks = 1.

cases.input: LeadGenix. Which channel gets the budget, SMS or email?
cases.right: SMS. Beats email ~8x on positive-per-send for this client.
cases.wrong: (plausible) Email, because raw reply rate looks higher.
cases.why: Positive-per-send + logged deals is the metric, not raw reply rate.

cases.input: DTCo. Write copy using the strongest available client logo.
cases.right: Does not use Grüns - it is a banned namedrop (Evergreen guideline: 'Gruns is OFF-LIMITS in DTCo copy').
cases.wrong: (plausible) Uses Grüns because it's the biggest name.
cases.why: Client-specific constraints must survive retrieval, which ranks by strength and will surface it.
